title: Getting started and signing in
summary: From signing in to your first brief.
steps: Sign in with an administrator-created account. If you have an invitation code, choose Register with invitation beside the sign-in heading to register in the same layout.
Check your name, phone and language preference in profile settings. Signed-in routes follow your account language preference.
Open Projects and choose New project. Creation requires permission and organization membership. Ask an administrator if the action is unavailable.
Complete book information, characters, voice, style, references and creative direction, then review and submit. Follow the steps and required-field prompts shown on screen.
You can open customer help from the sign-in page without signing in. Administration documentation requires a signed-in account with admin access.

Search help for “Invitation registration” for detailed steps and troubleshooting. Existing users can choose Forgot password below the password field, or expand Other login methods below the sign-in button.

faq.question: Can I register myself?
faq.answer: Registration requires a valid organization invitation code. The code determines your organization and grants a customer member account. Existing accounts should sign in; invitations cannot move them to another organization. Third-party login still requires an existing linked platform account.

title: Invitation registration and email verification
summary: Enter your display name, email and organization code, verify your email, then set a password and register.
steps: Ask an administrator for your organization’s invitation code. New codes contain 6 letters and are case-insensitive; previously issued long codes still work.

Choose Register with invitation beside the sign-in heading. Enter a display name (2–100 characters), email and invitation code together, then select Verify email. Register remains disabled and no account exists yet.
Check the organization shown on the page. If it is wrong, contact the administrator before continuing. Check your inbox and spam folder and open the verification link.

The link is valid for 10 minutes. It restores your display name and email and shows that the email is verified. The email is read-only. Set and confirm a password of 8–128 characters, then select Register.
After the account-created confirmation, select Sign in and use your new email and password. The account joins the invitation’s organization as a customer member.
To receive email notifications, enable them and choose topics in profile settings. Invitation registration verifies your email but does not automatically enable notifications.

faq.question: Does Verify email create my account?
faq.answer: No. Sending the email, opening the verification link and selecting Register are separate steps. Registration is complete only after the account-created confirmation.

faq.question: What if the email does not arrive?
faq.answer: Check spelling, spam and mail rules. Retry after 60 seconds. The response does not reveal whether an account already exists. Existing users should sign in or recover their password; otherwise ask an administrator to check the mail queue.

faq.question: What if the verification link no longer works?
faq.answer: Return to invitation registration and request another email. An expired link, expired or disabled invitation, inactive organization, exhausted capacity or existing email account can prevent registration.

faq.question: Can I correct my email after verification?
faq.answer: No. Verification proves ownership only of the email associated with that link. Return to invitation registration and request verification for the correct email.

faq.question: Does requesting verification reserve a slot?
faq.answer: No. A slot is consumed only when an account is successfully created. If several people compete for the last slot, only one registration succeeds. Others need to contact the administrator.

faq.question: Can an existing account use an invitation to join another organization?
faq.answer: No. Invitations create new customer accounts; they cannot move existing accounts or increase their permissions. Contact an administrator.

title: Preparing a brief and uploading files
summary: Enter book and creative information and verify uploads.
steps: Select the cover, full book or excerpt, and supplementary images in the book-upload step. Expand optional sections; field help shows supported formats and limits.
Fill required fields such as the book title, then choose characters, narration and visual style. Review presets against the actual book before submitting.
An upload at 100% may still be processing. Confirm that the file appears in the saved list. Failed files can be retried individually.
If book recognition is enabled, start it explicitly to assist entry. Check the result yourself; uploading does not start recognition automatically.

faq.question: Does cancelling an upload delete the file?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. Cancelling a transfer does not delete a file already saved. Check the list and use its delete action if needed.

faq.question: What if storage is full?
faq.answer: Ask an administrator to review storage. Avoid repeatedly uploading; existing downloads remain available, and files referenced by history may not release space immediately.

title: Draft saving, conflicts and duplication
summary: Recover unfinished work and duplicate your own project.
steps: Watch the save status and confirm success before leaving. Keep the page open if the network fails and check connectivity first.
For a version conflict, compare the latest version, select which fields to keep, then apply and continue editing.
For a similar brief, use Duplicate as new draft in your project actions. Review the new draft and files before submitting; the previous workflow state is not continued.

faq.question: Will refreshing recover unsaved input?
faq.answer: No guarantee. Conflict comparisons and upload queues live in page memory. Copy important unsaved text before loading the latest state.

faq.question: Can I duplicate a colleague’s project?
faq.answer: Organization sharing grants read access. Duplication, editing and deletion remain creator actions.

title: Submitting and confirming a brief
summary: Review required fields and confirm submission.
steps: Check completion on Review and submit. Follow validation links to fill missing required information.
Submit when ready and wait for a receipt or updated project status. Submitted material is no longer freely editable as a draft.
If the result is uncertain, use the result-check action or inspect the current project state before retrying.

faq.question: Does submission automatically produce a video?
faq.answer: Submission hands the brief to the team for follow-up. The platform does not promise automatic video production.

title: Handling requested changes and replies
summary: Update the requested sections and resubmit.
steps: Open your project from Pending or a notification. Read the reason and the sections opened for revision.
Edit the allowed fields and add a reply when needed. Read-only fields are outside this revision; do not create a replacement project simply to bypass them.
Resubmit as prompted and check the new status. Other organization members can read but cannot edit or reply on the creator’s behalf.

faq.question: Why can I edit only some fields?
faq.answer: A return may reopen only selected steps. Contact the project team through the available project communication channel if additional sections need changing.

title: Tracking progress and downloading deliverables
summary: Check project status and published deliverables.
steps: Open the project detail to see current progress. Expand information panels to review submitted material.
Use the delivery section to download published files. Preparing means there is no published deliverable available yet.
If a download fails, check your session and connection, then reopen the project. Withdrawal or a membership change can invalidate an old link.
When you enter details from a filtered project list, the return action preserves search, status, sorting and page. A detail link without a list source returns to the default list.

faq.question: Why is a completed project missing a file?
faq.answer: Project completion and publishing a deliverable are separate actions. Ask the project team whether the file has been published.

title: Organization sharing and member profiles
summary: Understand read access and creator-only actions.
steps: Open My organization, search for a member and select their avatar or name to view the available profile and activity.
Members of the same organization can read projects, materials and files, including drafts. The creator column identifies ownership and links to the creator’s profile.
Only the creator can edit, delete, submit or reply to their project. Pending actions concern your own work, not actions you must perform for colleagues.

faq.question: Can I still see projects after leaving an organization?
faq.answer: Shared access is rechecked against current membership. Colleague projects may disappear after a change; your own projects follow your personal permissions.

faq.question: Can I browse another organization?
faq.answer: Customer member links do not grant cross-organization access. Check your account and membership if an entry is unavailable.

title: Using the overview and activity calendar
summary: Switch between personal and organization scope and explore activity by date.
steps: Open Overview and select Personal or Organization, then choose a month. Personal covers your projects; Organization covers accessible organization projects. Calendar intensity reflects activity count; select a day for details.
Select a trend point or an actionable status item to inspect activity or open a filtered project list. Interactive controls also support keyboard focus.
Keep scope, month and project filters consistent when comparing counts. Historical coverage can be incomplete; absent records do not always mean no activity occurred.

faq.question: Why do overview and list counts differ?
faq.answer: Check Personal or Organization scope, month and list filters first. Organization statistics do not grant permission to edit colleagues’ projects.

title: Verifying email and enabling reminders
summary: Choose completion, revision, delivery and reply reminders.
steps: In profile settings, request an email verification message and confirm verification on the linked page. Links expire; use the newest message.
After verification, separately enable email notifications and select completion, requested changes, delivery, replies and other desired categories.
In-app notifications and email reminders are separate. Disabling email keeps in-app notifications; enabling it does not replay all historical notifications.

faq.question: Why are there no reminders after verification?
faq.answer: Verification does not subscribe you. Check the master switch and categories. The administrator must enable email service, and already-read notifications may no longer trigger reminders.

faq.question: What if email never arrives?
faq.answer: Check the address, spam folder and inbox rules, then wait briefly. Avoid repeated requests. Ask an administrator to inspect email status without sharing passwords or app credentials.

faq.question: Do I need to verify again after invitation registration?
faq.answer: Successful invitation registration already verifies your email. You still need to enable email notifications and select topics to receive reminders.

title: Password recovery and signed-in devices
summary: Recover through verified email and review sessions.
steps: Select Forgot password beside the remember-me option below the password field, then enter your account email. The response does not reveal whether the email is registered.
Open the newest recovery message, enter a new password and confirm. A successful reset invalidates previous sessions; sign in again.
Review signed-in devices in profile settings and revoke unfamiliar or unused sessions. Never forward recovery links.

faq.question: What if my email was never verified?
faq.answer: Self-service recovery does not send reset links to unverified addresses. Contact the platform owner for help.

faq.question: What if a link is invalid?
faq.answer: Links are single-use and expire. Changing email or password may invalidate them. Request a new link from the original entry point.

faq.question: Why does a remembered account require sign-in?
faq.answer: Remembered identities are separate from login sessions. Expiry, password changes or revocation require password verification again and never restore access automatically. Normal sign-out ends only the current session. Clear all accounts removes the list and signs out. Clearing browser cookies or using another browser requires adding accounts again.

title: Linking and using other sign-in methods
summary: Link an existing account to an enabled identity provider.
steps: Sign in with your platform password first. In profile settings, select a provider to link and confirm your current platform password.
Complete provider authorization and verify the linked state after returning. Later, choose that provider under Other sign-in options.
Providers are linked and unlinked separately. External roles do not automatically grant platform administration; platform permissions remain independently assigned.

faq.question: Can I still sign in if linking fails?
faq.answer: Platform-password sign-in and email recovery remain available. The provider may be disabled or misconfigured; contact an administrator rather than repeating authorization.

title: Reporting platform issues and reading replies
summary: Send reproduction steps and an optional screenshot; read replies in notifications.
steps: Open Feedback in the top bar, choose a category and describe the page, reproduction steps, expected outcome and actual result.
Use Choose image for an optional PNG, JPEG or WebP screenshot up to 10 MB before compression. Hide credentials and unrelated personal data.
After submitting, watch in-app notifications. Administrator replies arrive there; platform feedback has no separate chat window.

faq.question: What should I do when a request fails?
faq.answer: Check connectivity and retry reading. For submission, reply or upload, verify whether the action already succeeded before repeating it. Report the visible error and time if it persists.

title: Reading and dismissing the announcement banner
summary: Read scrolling content and manage account-level dismissal.
steps: Eligible notices appear above customer pages after sign-in. The banner scrolls both title and body. Select it for full details or choose View all for announcement history.
Hover or focus with the keyboard to pause, or use the pause/resume control. Reduced-motion preferences show static content.
Use the banner close button to hide that notice for your account across refreshes, sign-ins and devices. Other members are unaffected and new notices may still appear.
Closing the details window does not dismiss the banner. Dismissed or expired notices remain in history; withdrawn notices are removed. Retry a failed dismissal as prompted.

faq.question: Why does my colleague see a different notice?
faq.answer: Language and organization targeting, expiry and individual dismissal affect visibility. The banner shows only the newest eligible undismissed notice.
